A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReNF research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison despite the revised title, substantial reformatting, and relocated material.

before.justification: v5 reports original forecasting experiments, component ablations, oracle-combination analyses, and repeated-seed results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v6 retains these original empirical results and adds seed-level forecasting results in Table 13.

M1.justification: The BDO recursion, ReNF-alpha/beta architectures, weighted time/frequency loss, EMA, and M4 adaptation are retained. Corrected horizon indices and clearer diagrams do not establish a change to the implemented procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same long-term datasets, six supplementary short-term datasets, M4 subsets, and PEMS03/08 scenarios. The added seed breakdown uses Electricity and ETTm1, which were already evaluated.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding long-term, short-term, M4/PEMS, and robustness comparisons. TimeDistill's citation year changes from 2025 to 2026, but its participation and scores remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported splits, forecasting horizons, look-back windows, metrics, optimizer, and hyperparameter searches are retained. Additional seed and statistical-test disclosures do not establish a revised evaluation design.

E4.justification: v6 Table 13 adds evidence about run-to-run stability on Electricity and ETTm1, extending Appendix F's robustness documentation. The existing component, depth, dropout, EMA, representation, and M4/PEMS analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v6 specifies a paired t-test for Table 12 and explains its rounded zero deviations and significance column; the five-run count was already present. Figure 9 newly discloses three-seed averaging, and Table 13 reports named seeds and horizon-level means and standard deviations. These additions do not establish increased runs for existing results.

E6.justification: The matched benchmark and ablation tables retain their numerical results. v6 Table 13 adds seed-level entries, such as Electricity's 96-step MSE values of 0.118, 0.117, and 0.119. v6 Figure 4 also reverses the with/without-EMA legend assignments relative to v5 Figure 5 while retaining the curves.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 and Appendix B.1 substantially revise the central guarantee from an existence/pointwise formulation to an expected-error bound for the ensemble average. v6 replaces the selected-realization argument and unjustified pointwise noise bound with Jensen's inequality and explicit expected noise and bias bounds. This changes the mathematical guarantee and repairs a central proof step, while retaining the independence assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the central claims: BDO combines AR-like structure with DO stability, EMA mitigates validation-test inconsistency, and a simple MLP outperforms recent complex models on nearly all benchmarks. The revised theoretical details do not redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: v6 expands the existing independence caveat and explicitly frames VRH as a motivating heuristic for BDO. It newly acknowledges that EMA's particularly strong gains for MLPs are not comprehensively understood, softens EMA's characterization from a necessary protocol to a useful tool, and qualifies claims about practically achievable oracle-inspired combinations.

D1.justification: v6 replaces the anonymous review-code link with a stated public GitHub repository and explicitly identifies the EMA shadow model as the model used for early stopping. Hardware, optimizer, and hyperparameter-search details are retained.

R1.justification: v6 adds weight-averaging references, FFORMA, and a paragraph distinguishing BDO from iterative refinement and self-conditioning. It removes the TimeMCL discussion and citation. The existing positioning relative to ensembles, N-BEATS/N-HiTS, and MNN remains largely intact.

P1.justification: v6 revises the title and selected explanatory passages, moves and expands Appendix H into main-text Section 5, reorders two ablation subsections, and replaces the separate reproducibility statement with revised end matter. Most prose and the main narrative sequence are retained.

P2.justification: v6 switches the main text to two columns and extensively rearranges displays. It redraws the architecture and chunk-head diagrams, revises legends and captions, adds Table 13, and merges v5 Figures 14–15 into Figure 12. The small DO/BDO cartoon and duplicate main-text forecast display are removed.

improvement.justification: v6 improves rigor through the expected-error proof correction in Appendix B.1, corrects the misleading EMA legend, and makes statistical reporting more transparent through Table 12's explanation and Table 13's seed-level results. These are meaningful but limited gains: the method and principal empirical evidence remain stable, and the independence-based theory still does not directly guarantee the behavior of dependent BDO forecasts.
